metadata.title: Boundary behavior for a singular quasi-linear elliptic equation

nodes.name: Main Theorem
assumptions: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded domain. Consider problem \eqref{prob} where $a:(0,+\infty)\to (0,+\infty)$ is a $C^1$ function bounded away from zero, $f:(0,+\infty)\to (0,+\infty)$ is a $C^1$ function, and there exist $a_0>0$, $f_0>0$ such that $\lim_{s\to 0^+} a(s)s^{2\mu}=a_0$ for some $0\leq \mu<1$, $\lim_{s\to 0^+} f(s)s^\gamma=f_0$ for some $\gamma>1$, and $2f'(s)a(s)\leq f(s)a'(s)$ for every $s>0$.
conclusions: Problem \eqref{prob} has a unique solution $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$ and there exist $\Gamma,\Gamma',\Gamma''>0$ with $\Gamma{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}\leq u(x)\leq \Gamma'{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$, $|Du(x)|\leq \Gamma''{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{(1-\gamma+2\mu)/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$ as ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)\to 0$. Moreover $u\in {\rm Lip}(\bar\Omega)$ if $1<\gamma\leq 1+2\mu$, $u\in C^{0,2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}(\bar\Omega)$ if $\gamma>1+2\mu$ and $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ if $\gamma<3-2\mu$.
nodes.label: main

nodes.name: Map ψ and function H
nodes.statement:
Let us consider the map $\psi:[0,+\infty)\to [0,+\infty)$ defined by
	$$
	\psi(s):=\int_0^s \frac{1}{\sqrt{2{\mathcal H}(\xi)}}d\xi,\qquad
	{\mathcal H}(s):=\int_s^{+\infty} h(\xi)d\xi,
	\,\,\quad\text{for $s>0$.}
	$$

nodes.name: Singular Quasi-Linear Elliptic Problem
assumptions: Ω ⊂ ℝ^N is a smooth bounded domain; a:(0,+∞)→(0,+∞) is a C^1 function bounded away from zero; f:(0,+∞)→(0,+∞) is a C^1 function; there exist a_0>0 and f_0>0 such that lim_{s→0+} a(s)s^{2μ}=a_0 for some 0≤μ<1, lim_{s→0+} f(s)s^γ=f_0 for some γ>1, and 2f'(s)a(s)≤f(s)a'(s) for every s>0.
conclusions: Find the existence, uniqueness, and boundary behavior of solutions to this singular quasi-linear elliptic boundary value problem.
nodes.label: prob

nodes.name: Cauchy Problem for Change of Variable
assumptions: a:(0,+∞)→(0,+∞) is a C^1 function bounded away from zero; g ∈ C^2((0,+∞)) ∩ C([0,+∞)).
conclusions: Find g satisfying this Cauchy problem, used as a change of variable to convert the quasi-linear problem into a semi-linear problem.
nodes.label: cauchy

nodes.name: Asymptotic Problem
assumptions: ℓ ≥ 0; g is the solution to the Cauchy problem; f:(0,+∞)→(0,+∞) is a C^1 function satisfying the given asymptotic conditions.
conclusions: Find the unique solution φ ∈ C([0,+∞)) ∩ C^2((0,+∞)) to this first-order ODE problem, which governs the asymptotic boundary behavior of solutions.
nodes.label: asympt-prob

nodes.name: Second Order Asymptotic Problem
assumptions: φ is a solution to the asymptotic problem; g is the solution to the Cauchy problem; a is a fixed positive constant.
conclusions: The solutions to the asymptotic problem locally solve this second order boundary value problem on (0,a].
